sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- CSC,Dharmendra Singh Chauhan,Kuldeep Singh Chauhan
Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.
Heard Sri Rakesh Ranjan Agarwal, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Suyash Agarwal, learned
counsel for the petitioners, Sri Dharmendra Singh Chauhan learned counsel appearing on behalf of
Bulandshahr Development Authority and perused the record.

The present petition is directed against the order dated 13.12.2022, passed by Prescribed Authority,
Bulandshahr Development Authority, Bulandshahr in the proceeding under Section 26A(4) of the U.P. Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973.

entities.text: U.P. Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This order is being challenged with the submission that the petitioners herein are purchasers of some portions of the plot in question namely Gata No. 643, which constitute of a building popularly known as 'Pili Kothi', by virtue of the sale deeds executed by the wife of Dharam Pal who was subsequent transferee of Dharama Pal, who according to the petitioners were having right, title and interest in the property in question on the date of the execution of the sale deeds.
The sale deed in favour of petitioner no. 1 was executed in the year 2006, whereas the sale deed in favour of petitioner no. 2 is of the year 2017.

sentences.text: In various paragraphs of the writ petition, it is sought to be submitted that Gata No. 643 though was acquired by the acquisition notifications issued in the year 1990 but the award for existing 'constructions' over the said has never been declared nor the compensation was received by the original owner.

The copy of the award dated 12.01.1995 has been placed before us to submit that on the objection raised by Devraj Singh son of Dharam Pal and other co-sharers of plot no. 643, the existing 'Abadi' was released, i.e. no award for the existing 'Abadi' over plot no. 643 was made.

The submission, thus, is that the building known as 'Pili Kothi' existing over plot no. 643 has been released from acquisition and no compensation for the same has been determined by the competent authority.

As against these submissions, the order impugned records that Gata No. 643/2, area 0-3-0 and Gata No. 643/3 Area 0-3-10, total area 981 sq. yards was acquired and compensation was received by Devraj son of Dharam Pal on 27.02.1998.

The Land Acquisition Reference No. 147 of 1995 was instituted by Devraj before the Court of Additional District Judge, Bulandshahr, wherein a compromise had been arrived on 27.06.2001 with regard to the excess compensation.

entities.text: Court of Additional District Judge, Bulandshahr
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is further stated that another Suit No. 947 of 2013 was filed by Devraj Singh against some private person,
wherein a fraudulent decree dated 03.04.2014 was obtained in a collusive manner by the parties therein from the court of Civil Judge, Bulandshahr.
On the basis of said decree, Devraj Singh had sold an area of 246 sq. meter of the house in question to the petitioner no. 1 Mahendra Singh son of Mewaram on 20.01.2015.

The sale deed dated 19.05.2017 was executed in favour of petitioner no. 2 namely Mohd. Umar son of Mohd. Shamim Khan on the basis of the said sale deed dated 20.01.2015 by Mahendra Singh son of Mewa Ram.
Further sale deeds were also executed pursuant thereto.
It is, thus, recorded in the order impugned that the house in question exists over the plot no. 643 and the entire area of plot no. 643 is recorded in the name of Bulandshahr Development Authority.

The sale deeds executed by Devraj, his mother and sisters were without any authority of law and no valid right, title or interest can be passed on the basis of the sale deeds which are void in nature.
It is also recorded in the order impugned that a Civil Suit No. 1273 of 2022 has been filed by the petitioners herein which is pending before the court of Civil Judge, Bulandshahr.

It is, thus,
recorded in the order impugned that the possession of the petitioners over the plot in question is of unauthorized occupants.

Taking note of all these facts, we are required to record that the acquisition notifications under the Land Acquisition Act, which have been placed before us by the counsel for the development authority are dated 30.03.1990 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act and dated 13.08.1990 under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act.
Section 4 notification which has been placed before us records the details of the property, the total area of 44.7688 hectares which was proposed to be acquired through the acquisition notifications.
It contains the details of plot nos. 643/1, Area 0.335 hectares and plot no. 643/2, Area 0.291 hectares.

Whereas, in the declaration notification under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, the details of three acquired plots bearing plots no. 643/1, area 1-6-10; 643/2, area 1-3-0 and 643/3, area 0-3-10 has been given.
The total area of the acquired land as per the declaration notification under Section 6 is 171-14-17, area 107.31 hectares.

sentences.text: 2 There is, thus, a variance in the description of plot no. 643 in the proposal notification under Section 4 and declaration notification under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act.
In the order impugned, there is a reference of plot no. 643/1 which was included in both the acquisition notifications under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The order impugned records that a report was called from the office of the Land Acquisition Officer,
Bulandshahr with regard to the payment of compensation for the acquired lands in Gata Nos. 643/1,
643/2 and 643/3 and in reply thereto, a copy of Form 11 was submitted by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, wherein it is indicated that the compensation for the existing building over Gata No. 643 was not received by Devraj Singh.

However, as per the report of the Sub Divisional Officer,
Special Land Acquisition Officer and a joint inspection report on the file of the Secretary,
Development Authority, there was no construction or building over plot no. 643.
From the facts noted above, it is more than evident that the acquisition of three plots which were numbered as Gata Nos. 643/1, 643/2 and 643/3, was made.
The total area of all these plots as per the declaration notification under Section 6 comes to 3-3-0.

However, as per the statement made in the order impugned itself the compensation was received by Devraj son of Dharampal Singh, the original owner of an area of 0-3-0 of Gata No. 643/2 and 0-3-10 of Gata No. 643/3 (total 0-6-10) area (981 sq. meters).

But there is no finding with regard to the receipt of compensation of Gata No. 643/1, area 1-6-10 indicated in the acquisition notification under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act dated 13.08.1990.
Moreover the total acquired area of Gata No. 643/2 was 1-3-0 whereas compensation for only an area of 0-3-0 was received by Devraj son of Dharampal Singh, the original owner.

The report submitted by the Land Acquisition Officer in Form 11 further indicates that no compensation for the house existing over Gata No. 643 was received by the original tenure holder i.e. Devraj Singh.

We, therefore, find substance in the submissions of the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners that the compensation for the existing building over the plot in question namely Gata No. 643 was not received by the original owner.

The dispute, thus, remains with regard to the acquisition of the building in question namely 'Pili Kothi'
which exists over plot no. 643.

The averments in the order impugned about the encroachment made by the petitioners and for illegal transfer of the existing building in favour of the petitioners, therefore, are required to be examined on the evidence of the rival parties.

The petitioners herein have filed a civil suit namely Original Suit No. 1273 of 2022, with regard to the property in question with the relief of permanent prohibitory injunction, which is pending before the Civil Court, Bulandshahr.
We, therefore, do not find any good ground to entertain the present writ petition.
It is kept open for the petitioners to seek appropriate relief in the pending suit by challenging the stand of the Development Authority taken in the order impugned dated 13.12.2022.

sentences.text: It is informed that the next date fixed in civil court is 09.02.2023 and the interim injunction application is pending consideration before it.

It is submitted by the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners that because of this application under Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C., filed by the Development Authority, the interim injunction application could not be decided.
The application under Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C. filed by the development authority has, however, been rejected.
Noticing the above, we provide that the petitioners may press the pending interim injunction application before the civil court by seeking appropriate relief of setting aside the order impugned.
in the pending suit.
It is expected that the civil court will decide the pending injunction application on the next date fixed i.e. 09.02.2023.
For the above noted facts, it is provided that there shall be no coercive action against the petitioners herein till the next date fixed in the pending suit before the civil court i.e. 09.02.2023.
It goes without saying that the civil court shall give independent consideration to the claims of the parties herein and shall not be guided by any of the observations made herein.
With the above observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
